subject: Custodial boundaries & evidentiary options for Private/VPC storage

From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@medicorp.com>

Cc: legal@medicorp.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 22:07:00 -0700
Subject: Residency and deletion evidence for Private VPC deployment

Hannah —

Thanks for the demo today. Before we proceed to procurement and a pilot, our security and privacy team need clarity on a few items for a Private (VPC) deployment where MediCorp retains control of storage:

1) What specific artifacts can Redwood provide to prove customer data is physically and logically resident in the customer's controlled bucket(s) and region? Examples we care about: storage URIs, region tags, bucket policies, access logs.
2) For retention and deletion, what evidence can you produce after a customer requests deletion? We need to see timelines (e.g., purge within X hours), proof of object removal, and a way to confirm KV/cache eviction for model context if applicable.
3) Key management: can you provide evidence that encryption keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) and that key destruction (or crypto-erase) is logged?
4) If we ever terminate, what handover or certificate-of-deletion artifacts do you produce? Is there an optional attestation for audit?

If you can outline the artifacts and an estimated timeline to produce them (and any limitations), that will help our InfoSec write the acceptance criteria.

Tom
Tom Hayes
Head of Cloud Security, MediCorp Health
From: hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@medicorp.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency and deletion evidence for Private VPC deployment

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list — this is exactly the level of detail we want to align on. At a high level, for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments where the customer controls the storage layer we can provide the following artifacts and timelines: 

- Storage residency: canonical list of storage endpoints and ARN-style identifiers (or provider URIs) tied to the tenant; confirmation of configured region tags and bucket-level policies. Delivery: initial report at onboarding; updated export on request (2 business days).

- Access/OPS logs: signed copies of access logs (S3 access logs / GCS access logs) for the buckets we touch; we can also provide service-side request logs showing our runtime nodes interacting only with customer-owned buckets. Delivery: historical slices available for export; on-request extracts within 3 business days.

- Deletion evidence: when a delete request is executed we provide: (a) object-level deletion manifest (list of keys removed), (b) storage provider deletion confirmation where available (e.g., S3 inventory/replication status), and (c) a post-action surfaced summary stating cache + prefix eviction actions we triggered at the runtime layer. Delivery: standard timeline is 5 business days for full evidentiary package; emergency wipes can be escalated.

- Key management: we support BYOK via customer KMS/HSM. We can provide KMS audit entries showing key usage and a KMS key-disable/destroy timeline for crypto-erase scenarios (subject to provider retention rules). Delivery: KMS audit exports available within 2 business days.

- Termination/handback: we produce a handover packet containing the final bucket inventory, deletion manifest, and a signed statement of actions taken. We also offer an optional independent attestation (third-party letter) for enterprise contracts — timeline depends on scope (typically 10–20 business days).

I’m looping in Rishi and Marissa (security + legal touchpoints) to confirm the technical/log artifacts and share a template evidence matrix we can attach. Would you prefer vendor-signed PDFs or direct Drive links in our initial reply?

—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Residency and deletion evidence for Private VPC deployment

Hannah —

Summary from security engineering (for the evidence matrix Hannah will share):

1) Storage residency artifacts we can reliably provide:
   - Tenant-targeted storage URIs (e.g., s3://mc-health-prod-tenant-8743) and the cloud region (e.g., us-west-2).
   - Bucket policy snapshots showing explicit denies/permits used by Redwood runtime IAM role.
   - Service-side access log excerpts evidencing only our runtime roles reading/writing to the tenant bucket during the observed timeframe.

2) Deletion/retention mechanics and evidence:
   - We execute deletions by removing objects from the customer bucket and triggering lifecycle rules where customers want provider-level purge. For immediate administrative deletes we generate a deletion manifest file and a signed hash (SHA256) of the manifest.
   - For KV/LLM runtime caches (in-memory and local SSD caching on inference nodes): we provide an eviction event log. Note: in-memory caches are ephemeral; we log the eviction command and the node IDs and timestamps.
   - If customer uses provider-side versioning/replication, final-state evidence will include provider inventory and replication lag notes. Provider retention policies may impose a short replication window before physical purge.

3) KMS/BYOK specifics:
   - BYOK supported via customer-managed KMS. We do not retain plaintext keys.
   - Key Disable/Destroy operations are recorded in KMS audit logs; we can export those entries. Note: actual key destruction cadence is subject to customer KMS policies and provider safety windows.

4) Timelines and SLAs:
   - Standard evidentiary package: 5 business days post-request.
   - Fast-track (for exec/contractual escalations): 48–72 hours subject to SOW.

I attached an evidence matrix and a short sample retention policy to this thread for MediCorp to review. Marissa, please confirm legal language for the termination attestation and the independent attestation option.

-Rishi
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
